relevance_note: Supplementary Table S1 gives individual-level data (age at VCE, sex, endoscopic and histologic findings, treatment) for five patients whose genotype is listed as "TNFAIP3" (Patients 2, 5, 9, 12 and 32), matching the text's "The frequent mutations were found in TNFAIP3 (n=5)".
method_note: Cohort of 37 VEOIBD patients; only the five with genotype TNFAIP3 in Table S1 are in scope (no relatives described). A Python script in my scratch directory cut Table S1 at fixed character columns (Case, Age at VCE, Gender, Genotype, Classification, Duodenum on VCE, Jejunum on VCE, Ileum on VCE, Colonic feature on colonoscopy, Ileal feature on colonoscopy, Gastric feature on gastroscopy, Duodenal bulb feature on gastroscopy, Descending part of the duodenum, Histology, Treatment); I checked every cell of the 13 TNFAIP3 rows against the table by eye. Multi-exam patients occupy one row per VCE; Gender, Genotype, Classification and Treatment are printed once per patient block (Gender in a different row from Genotype), which I read as merged cells applying to the whole patient. Ages are the printed 'Age at VCE'; the unit (years) is inferred from the text's average age at VCE in years, and age_at_last_evaluation is the age at the patient's last listed VCE. No age at onset or diagnosis is given per patient (VEOIBD's definition of onset before 6 years was not used, being a study criterion). No variant description, zygosity or inheritance is printed for any TNFAIP3 patient, so variant rows have variant_original_string 'not reported'; pathogenicity 'pathogenic' rests on the group-level Figure 1 caption ('patients with identified pathogenic variants') and the statement that sequencing confirmed known monogenic IBD. ethnicity_or_country 'China' is the study country (patients identified at five Chinese centres), not a stated ancestry. Phenotypic rows: one per (patient, Table S1 column, lesion term) aggregated over the patient's exams; lesion terms split at commas, with the typo 'edmea' read as edema. At most three rows are quoted per feature, so findings seen on four exams list only the first three in severity_or_detail (Patient 2 edema (Ileum on VCE) also on Patient 2 VCE 4; Patient 2 erosion (Colonic feature on colonoscopy) also on Patient 2 VCE 4; Patient 2 edema (Gastric feature on gastroscopy) also on Patient 2 VCE 4; Patient 2 Chronic active enteritis (Histology) also on Patient 2 VCE 4; Patient 12 ulcer (Jejunum on VCE) also on Patient 12 VCE 4; Patient 12 erosion (Ileal feature on colonoscopy) also on Patient 12 VCE 4; Patient 12 edema (Gastric feature on gastroscopy) also on Patient 12 VCE 4; Patient 12 normal (Descending part of the duodenum) also on Patient 12 VCE 4; Patient 12 Chronic active enteritis (Histology) also on Patient 12 VCE 4). 'normal' cells were used as 'excluded' only when that column was normal at every exam of the patient; a 'normal' cell at one exam with lesions at another was not recorded. Empty and 'NA' cells are not reported. Checklist: only gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation is addressed per patient; recurrent infections are given only as a cohort count (4 patients), so not reported. Group statements not used per person: 'All patients with TNFAIP3 mutations except one suffered from ileal ulcers', 'Patients with TNFAIP3 mutations also had colonic erosions and ulcers', the persistence statement, and Figure 2/4 legends (Figure 4 D-F, 'Another patient with TNFAIP3 mutations, her small lesions did not improve during 4 years of follow-up', is not labelled with a case number). Prior reports: the paper says it extends an ESPGHAN e-Poster (recorded as the prior report; an e-Poster may not be a formal publication); it also cites the group's prior work (7,8) and a prior TNFAIP3 IBD paper (30) from overlapping authors without saying the same patients are included. Contradictions/inconsistencies: by VCE alone, two TNFAIP3 patients (5 and 32) show no ileal ulcer, although the text says all except one had ileal ulcers (both have ileal ulcers on colonoscopy); 18/37 monogenic is given as 48.6% but the Discussion says 45%; 58 VCE procedures are stated but Table 1 counts 55; 'Twelve patients' had follow-up VCE but the breakdown (1+5+5) sums to 11, and Table S1 shows three patients with four VCEs.
